subject: Tidy data: calculating the difference in a measurement between control and treatments

messages.author: bbea236abe87368e
messages.subject: Tidy data: calculating the difference in a measurement between control and treatments
parts:
Hi all,

I have a question that I feel should have a simple answer, but all of my current solutions are overly complicated.

I have a dataframe with one column for treatment (‘control’, ‘a’, ‘b’) and then a couple columns of a measurement (‘height’, ‘width’). There’s also a column for sample ID which is consistent across the treatments (‘1’, ‘2’, ‘3’—all of which appear in all three treatments and have each measurement).

I’d like to calculate the difference between the height in the control treatment and the height in each treatment for each of my samples. In a wide format this would be easy—I’d have separate columns for height.control and height.a, and I would just subtract one from the other and make a new column height.difference. For tidy data, my initial thought was to do something like with(df, height[treatment==‘a’] - height[treatment==‘control’]) but I’m not sure how to incorporate multiple treatments (‘a’ to control and ‘b’ to control). Also this assumes my sample IDs are in consistent order, which they are in this case but a more general approach could also be better. I want to save this output as another column, not additional rows—something like ‘height.difference’ which would be 0 for the control rows and non-zero for the other treatment rows.

input
sample.id treatment height width
1 control 2 3
2 control 1 1
1 a 2 1
2 a 2 2
1 b 3 3
2 b 2 4

desired output
sample.id treatment height width height.diff width.diff
1 control 2 3 0 0
2 control 1 1 0 0
1 a 2 1 0 -2
2 a 2 2 1 1
1 b 3 3 1 0
2 b 2 4 1 3

Thanks for your ideas and help! This is such a simple thing that I’m not even sure how to search for examples online.

Chhaya

messages.author: 5f533b50135a7f86
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Tidy data: calculating the difference in a measurement between control and treatments
parts:
Hi Chhaya, 

In the tidy data paradigm, each row is supposed to correspond to an “observation” — which isn’t a single measurement, but "all values measured on the same unit (like a person, or a day, or a race) across attributes” (https://tidyr.tidyverse.org/dev/articles/tidy-data.html).  But what counts as a single unit depends on your research question, the way you’re analyzing your data, and so on.  This can even be different *within* your analysis.  Data can be tidy for one step of your analysis (say, graphing height vs treatment in ggplot) and "too long” for another step (say, taking differences across treatments).  I think this is a point we don’t talk about enough when we talk about long vs. wide data and functions like spread() or gather().  

Okay, setting aside the philosophy, you need to use some tools to make your data wider.  To do this for height and width at the same time, you’ll need to use the new pivot_wider() function (https://tidyr.tidyverse.org/dev/articles/pivot.html).  Since I haven’t switched to that yet, and I only have a couple of minutes to write this email, I’m going to explain how to do it using spread().  But that means doing it separately for height and width.  

Here’s what it looks like for height:  
height_diff_df = df %>% 
select(sample.id, treatment, height) %>%
spread(key = treatment, value = height) %>%
mutate(height.a.diff = a - treatment, 
    height.b.diff = b - treatment)

Then do it the same way for width.  If you want, put the two data frames back together using a join (e.g., left_join(height_diff_df, weight_diff_df, by = c(’sample.id’, ’treatment’)).  

Dan

messages.author: d0c629ef4df1de7c
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Tidy data: calculating the difference in a measurement between control and treatments
parts:
Your suspicion that it is simple is correct :) No need for any pivoting / reshaping here. In base R you can do this:

d$height.diff = d$height - d[d$treatment == "control", "height"]

R's vector recycling rules will do the right thing here IF:
1. the data is sorted correctly: d = d[order(d$treatment, d$sample.id), ]
2. Each sample.id has the same number of treatments

For your example:

d = read.table(header = TRUE, text = "sample.id  treatment  height  width
+ 1                  control               2           3
+ 2                  control               1           1
+ 1                  a                          2          1
+ 2                 a                           2          2
+ 1                  b                         3          3
+ 2                 b                          2          4")
> d$height.diff = d$height - d[d$treatment == "control", "height"]
> d$width.diff = d$width - d[d$treatment == "control", "width"]
> d
sample.id treatment height width height.diff width.diff

1         1   control      2     3           0          0
2         2   control      1     1           0          0
3         1         a      2     1           0         -2
4         2         a      2     2           1          1
5         1         b      3     3           1          0
6         2         b      2     4           1          3

Best,
Clark
